**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Mechanics, Paper 3 (0765/3), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2025. Duration: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. All questions carry equal marks. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.
enonce_intro_markdown:
A block $P$ of mass $4\ \mathrm{kg}$ lies on a plane inclined at an angle of $60^\circ$ to the horizontal. It is connected to another block $Q$ of mass $6\ \mathrm{kg}$ which hangs freely by means of a light inextensible string passing over a smooth fixed pulley at the top of the plane.

(Take $g$ as $10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$)
incertitudes: Question 3 : le sujet n'imprime aucune figure ; le schéma (plan incliné, poulie en haut du plan, Q suspendu) est décrit dans le corrigé. Le sujet imprime « Take g as 10 m s^-2 » : cette valeur est utilisée. Dans la question (b), la mention du coefficient de frottement concerne P et le plan ; le sens du mouvement (Q descend, P monte) est vérifié par le calcul (60 N > 20 racine(3) + 12 N).

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the acceleration of the system and the tension in the string if the plane is smooth.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Diagram (described).** $P$ ($4\ \mathrm{kg}$) is on the plane inclined at $60^\circ$ to the horizontal; the string is parallel to the line of greatest slope, runs up to the smooth pulley at the top of the plane and hangs vertically down to $Q$ ($6\ \mathrm{kg}$). Take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ (printed). Forces on $P$: tension $T$ up the slope, weight $4g = 40\ \mathrm{N}$ vertically downwards, normal reaction $R$ perpendicular to the plane. Forces on $Q$: tension $T$ upwards, weight $6g = 60\ \mathrm{N}$ downwards.

**Direction of motion.** The weight of $Q$ is $60\ \mathrm{N}$, whereas the component of the weight of $P$ down the slope is $40\sin 60^\circ = 20\sqrt{3} \approx 34.6\ \mathrm{N}$. Since $60 > 34.6$, $Q$ moves down and $P$ moves up the slope. Take that as the positive direction, with common acceleration $a$ (the string is inextensible and the pulley is smooth, so the tension $T$ and the acceleration are the same on both sides).

**Equations of motion** (Newton's second law):

For $Q$ (downwards):
$$60 - T = 6a$$

For $P$ (up the slope, smooth plane so no friction):
$$T - 40\sin 60^\circ = 4a \;\Rightarrow\; T - 20\sqrt{3} = 4a$$

**Adding** eliminates $T$:

$$60 - 20\sqrt{3} = 10a \;\Rightarrow\; a = 6 - 2\sqrt{3} \approx 2.54\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$$

**Tension:** $T = 60 - 6a = 60 - 36 + 12\sqrt{3} = 24 + 12\sqrt{3} \approx 44.8\ \mathrm{N}$.

**Check** with $P$: $T = 4a + 20\sqrt{3} = 24 - 8\sqrt{3} + 20\sqrt{3} = 24 + 12\sqrt{3}$.

**Acceleration $= 6 - 2\sqrt{3} \approx 2.54\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; tension $= 24 + 12\sqrt{3} \approx 44.8\ \mathrm{N}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the acceleration of the system and the tension in the string if the plane is rough and the coefficient of friction between $P$ and the plane is $\dfrac{3}{5}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Forces.** As in part (a), with $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ (printed), plus friction on $P$.

**Normal reaction.** Perpendicular to the plane, $P$ is in equilibrium: $R = 4g\cos 60^\circ = 40\times\tfrac12 = 20\ \mathrm{N}$.

**Maximum friction:** $F_{\max} = \mu R = \tfrac35\times 20 = 12\ \mathrm{N}$.

**Does the system move?** The driving force for the motion "$Q$ down, $P$ up" is $60\ \mathrm{N}$ and the resistance to it is at most $20\sqrt{3} + 12 \approx 34.6 + 12 = 46.6\ \mathrm{N}$. Since $60 > 46.6$ the system does move, with $Q$ descending and $P$ moving up the slope; friction opposes the motion of $P$, so it acts **down** the slope and is limiting: $F = 12\ \mathrm{N}$.

**Equations of motion** (positive: $P$ up the slope, $Q$ down):

For $Q$:
$$60 - T = 6a$$

For $P$:
$$T - 20\sqrt{3} - 12 = 4a$$

**Adding:**

$$60 - 20\sqrt{3} - 12 = 10a \;\Rightarrow\; a = \frac{48 - 20\sqrt{3}}{10} = \frac{24}{5} - 2\sqrt{3} \approx 1.34\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$$

**Tension:** $T = 60 - 6a = 60 - \dfrac{144}{5} + 12\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{156}{5} + 12\sqrt{3} \approx 52.0\ \mathrm{N}$.

**Check** with $P$: $T = 4a + 20\sqrt{3} + 12 = 19.2 - 8\sqrt{3} + 20\sqrt{3} + 12 = 31.2 + 12\sqrt{3}$.

**Acceleration $= \dfrac{24}{5} - 2\sqrt{3} \approx 1.34\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; tension $= \dfrac{156}{5} + 12\sqrt{3} \approx 52.0\ \mathrm{N}$.**
